name: USDA ERS Food Environment Atlas (selected county measures)
publisher: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Economic Research Service (ERS)
source_release_id: Food Environment Atlas July 2025 release (CSV files, last updated 7/30/2025)

release_markers.readme_release_sentence: The original release date of this file is July 2025.

downloads_page: "No data" fields are referenced with N/A or with -9999. Counties that didn’t exist in a particular year are referenced with -8888.
documentation: Counties that didn’t exist in a particular year are referenced with -8888.
county-boundary updates in the Food Environment Atlas are applied in 5-year intervals, with county boundaries corresponding to the 2010, 2015, and 2020 Census Bureau updates.
The year 2023 county boundaries are included as an exception to reflect Connecticut’s transition from counties to planning regions.
In 2019, Valdez-Cordova Census Area, AK (02261) was split into Chugach Census Area, AK (02063) and Copper River Census Area, AK (02066).
In 2022, Connecticut transitioned from eight counties to nine planning regions.
Percentage of people in a county with low income and living more than 1 mile from a foodstore if in an urban area, or more than 10 miles from a foodstore if in a rural area.
That number was divided by the total number of individuals in the county to obtain the percentage of total population in the county that resided more than 1 or 10 miles from a foodstore.
Low-income is defined as annual family income of less than or equal to 200 percent of the Federal poverty threshold based on family size.
The average monthly number of stores in the county authorized to accept SNAP per 1,000 county residents.
ERS did not include meal service providers that serve eligible persons among SNAP-authorized stores during calculation of this variable.
The number of stores in a county that are authorized to accept WIC benefits per 1,000 population.
The number of farmers' markets in the county per 1,000 county residents.
Information included in the Directory is voluntary and self-reported to AMS by market managers
Percentage of housing units in a county that are without a car and more than 1 mile from a foodstore.
That number was divided by the total number of housing units in the county to obtain the percentage of housing units in the county that were more than 1 mile from a foodstore and without a vehicle.
readme: Counties that didn’t exist in a particular year are referenced with -8888.
Indicators are measured at the county level unless noted with an asterisk (*), which signifies a State-level measure.

state_values: none: the July 2025 files contain no state rows, and none of the selected variables is marked as a State-level (*) measure. State-level (*) variables in this file are repeated on every county row and are not used.

boundary.join_rule: Exact five-character text FIPS from the USDA file equals the TIGER/Line 2024 county GEOID. No reassignment, splitting, or merging of counties.
boundary.source_vintage_note: USDA applies county boundaries at 5-year intervals (2010, 2015, 2020 Census updates). The 2019, 2022, and 2023 selected measures use 2020-vintage counties, including Connecticut's eight former counties; the 2018 farmers' market measure uses pre-2019 counties (Valdez-Cordova, AK). Outside Connecticut and Valdez-Cordova, these FIPS codes are unchanged in TIGER/Line 2024.

measures.variable_name: Low income & low access to store (%), 2019
measures.label: Low-income residents with low supermarket access (share of all residents)
measures.denominator: Total county population (2010 Census block population). The numerator is low-income residents only.
measures.official_definition: Percentage of people in a county with low income and living more than 1 mile from a foodstore if in an urban area, or more than 10 miles from a foodstore if in a rural area.
measures.contributing_sources: ERS Low-Income and Low-Foodstore-Access Census Tracts, 2015–19: SNAP-authorized supermarkets merged with NielsenIQ TDLinx (stores with at least $2 million in sales and all major food departments); 2010 Census block population; 2014–18 ACS income. Low income means family income at or below 200% of the poverty threshold.
measures.interpretation: Share of all county residents who are low income and live beyond 1 mile (urban) or 10 miles (rural) from a supermarket or large grocery store. Not a food-desert designation, not a measure of diet quality, and based on 2019 store locations.

measures.label: SNAP-authorized stores per 1,000 residents
measures.official_definition: The average monthly number of stores in the county authorized to accept SNAP per 1,000 county residents.
measures.contributing_sources: USDA Food and Nutrition Service, SNAP Benefits Redemption Division (store authorizations); Census Bureau population estimates. Excludes meal service providers.
measures.interpretation: Authorized retailers of all types: supermarkets, grocery and convenience stores, supercenters, warehouse clubs, and specialty food stores. Retailer authorization does not indicate the healthfulness of foods sold. A 2023 average, not a current store directory.

measures.label: WIC-authorized stores per 1,000 residents
measures.official_definition: The number of stores in a county that are authorized to accept WIC benefits per 1,000 population.
measures.contributing_sources: USDA Food and Nutrition Service, Supplemental Food Programs Division, Program Analysis and Monitoring Branch; Census Bureau population estimates. Mississippi WIC direct distribution centers are not stores.
measures.interpretation: Stores authorized to accept WIC benefits. Authorization does not indicate the foods stocked or diet quality. A 2022 count, not a current store directory.

measures.label: Farmers' markets per 1,000 residents
measures.official_definition: The number of farmers' markets in the county per 1,000 county residents.
measures.contributing_sources: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service, National Farmers Market Directory (voluntary, self-reported listings); Census Bureau population estimates.
measures.interpretation: Markets listed in a voluntary, self-reported directory in 2018. Zero means no market was listed, not that none operated. Not a current market directory.
measures.source_boundary_basis: Pre-2019 counties (Valdez-Cordova, AK; Connecticut's former counties)

measures.variable_name: Households, no car & low access to store (%), 2019
measures.label: Housing units with no car and low supermarket access
measures.denominator: Total county housing units. USDA's variable label says households; its definition uses housing units.
measures.official_definition: Percentage of housing units in a county that are without a car and more than 1 mile from a foodstore.
measures.contributing_sources: ERS Low-Income and Low-Foodstore-Access Census Tracts, 2015–19: SNAP-authorized supermarkets merged with NielsenIQ TDLinx; 2014–18 ACS household vehicle availability.
measures.interpretation: Substitute for grocery-store density. Uses a single 1-mile distance for every county, urban or rural. Not a food-desert designation and based on 2019 store locations.

excluded_targets.GROCPTH20: Grocery stores/1,000 pop, 2020 (County Business Patterns, NAICS 445110) duplicates the published AHRQ CLH measure CCBP_SOGS_RATE (same CBP NAICS 445110 per-1,000 concept, newer 2023 observation), and 909 of 3,144 counties are -9999 in this file.
excluded_targets.DSPTH20: Labelled 'Dollar stores' in the variable list, but documented as all NAICS 452319 general merchandise stores; not used.
